How to avoid overheating while fuel scooping?

It's all about positioning. The key is to keep an eye on your temperature the closer you get to the source. There is a nice little sweetspot that you can stay in pretty much forever whilst you top up. Of course; like much of Elite: Dangerous; there is a risk/reward to fuel scooping. If you're in a dangerous place, you can scoop faster; but you risk setting fire to yourself in the progress! It's a good idea to practice your scoops in an uninhabited system first. Good luck!

My approach is to approach the sun head on until your scoop is working at maximum capacity. When doing this, you need to approach slowly as there is a sweet spot, as Anther said, where you can scoop efficiently without overheating. I usually leave my ship facing the star and keep my FSD speed to the minimum allowed (30km/s). This is usually a good time to take a look at your galactic or system map, check trade routes, read news, go for a tea/coffee refill, bath break etc. (the latter two are at your own risk if in dangerous space!)
That's a good point about setting your speed to minimum! I'd completely forgotten to mention that.
Also if you buy a better fuel scoop you don't have to go as near as with a smaller one. And as usual. Practice, practice, practice.

While positioning is crucial, the best piece of advice I can give you is to buy a better fuel scoop.

I prefer to orbit the star while refueling, adjusting my pitch to the sweet spot where I'm not taking any heat, but still scooping reasonably quickly. The glow of the star will just be visible at the bottom of your cockpit view.

Orbiting does two things, it keeps me moving, and it allows me to line up with my next jump point at the same time. Again, a good scoop will allow you to scoop far more efficiently.

I fly around the star. You can watch the heat rise if it get's too hot you can back off a bit. After a while you can tell by looking at the light coming off the star as you fly around it how far you need to be. You need to fly a certain direction so you're able to look up at the star but don't have the star in sight only the light coming from it should be visible when doing this. And like others have said save up for a bigger scoop. I myself saved up for a better ship with more fuel capacity so I don't need the scoop for now...but that's another story.
